feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond scale, and has a few style/grammar consistency issues.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression with increasing responsibility at one organization, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong domain fit: digital strategy, Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: include measurable results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign impact, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a tighter structure and more scannable CV.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“workflows, and systems” vs no serial comma elsewhere); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding public-sector/advocacy relevance would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Add sector specificity: emphasize public-sector, membership, or advocacy organizations to better match the work history.
- Reduce broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) and focus on differentiators like platform modernization, editorial systems, and technical/policy translation.
- Possible rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience advancing web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital governance. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, audience-focused content and aligning stakeholders around effective advocacy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also reappear in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize distinctive, high-value capabilities rather than broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned wording: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Drupal/CMS platform management.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items: combine “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” into one stronger competency.
- Prioritize recent, higher-level strengths from recent roles: digital transformation, CMS modernization, analytics/insights, governance, and advocacy communications.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Drupal/CMS platform management • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Public-sector policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items repeat Topline Skills almost verbatim, especially digital strategy, analytics, and multimedia.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with impact and seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel content operations for a national membership organization.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 sharper points focused on outcomes: digital systems/workflows/analytics; Drupal campaign builds; governance/usability; AI-enabled search initiative.
- Replace generic phrasing like “deliver CMS development” and “advise on best practices” with stronger verbs: “implemented,” “optimized,” “standardized,” “designed,” “launched.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search relevance gains, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance/usability across channels” repeat the 2022–2024 Director role; frame this as post-tenure consulting support or new initiatives.
- Microsite/toolkit details and AI search are already in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Make the website bullet the anchor achievement: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Recast channel oversight toward leadership/outcomes, not routine management: “Oversaw enterprise email and social strategy reaching tens of thousands of county officials; aligned channels with advocacy, member engagement, and organizational priorities.”
- Combine studio/analytics/governance into concise impact bullets, adding measurable results if available (production volume, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, cost savings, reduced publishing errors).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current email/social/video wording overlaps with Associate Communications Director.
- “Built first in-house video studio” may partially overlap with footer project examples; keep this entry at leadership level.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level and emphasize scale, cadence, and cross-functional coordination.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete responsibilities: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show build-out and repeatability: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper outcome-oriented line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing coordination and consistency across digital channels.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here to preserve seniority progression.
- Video-series language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; avoid claiming this as the first launch unless accurate.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the most senior, differentiating strengths and use tighter phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy campaigns & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, storytelling & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with your recent roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one skill to scale/results rather than listing only abstractions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat software lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older-sounding items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Use “enterprise CMS platforms” or “digital platform implementation” to sound more senior than a raw list of products.
- If possible, align wording to recent impact: “Drupal-led modernization,” “platform integrations,” or “AI-enabled search experiences” tied to current consulting/director work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI framework design, executive dashboarding, user behavior analysis, SEO/performance insights.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the capability terms: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards.”
- If accurate, add an outcome-oriented qualifier such as “decision-ready reporting” or “measurement frameworks for web modernization and campaign performance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item duplicates almost exactly with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic capabilities and leave the full tool stack there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may also overlap with broader digital strategy language unless framed as analytics-specific.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-level production capability and current relevance rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented, senior-level skills: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the in-house studio achievement.
- Tighten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid/virtual event delivery” for concision and consistency with the heading.
- If accurate, add scale or complexity in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., recurring programs, in-house studio build, advocacy/event coverage).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already evidenced in the Director/Associate roles, so this skills line should stay concise and non-repetitive.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a generic list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (primary)** • WordPress (working) • SharePoint/Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages
- Consider tightening the title to **CMS & Web Platforms** for clearer alignment with the content.
- If you want more impact, replace one lower-priority platform with a capability: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • CMS migration/governance**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus stronger context.
- Avoid repeating all five platforms in both sections unless one version adds proficiency or business context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and selective.

Suggested edit
- Reframe as a tighter, modern stack: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group tools by use case to improve scanability: “Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- If accurate, add scope or level to avoid sounding entry-level, e.g., “custom front-end fixes,” “light scripting,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless edge functions”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless they matter; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the stronger version in one place
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere, so GitHub Actions should be framed specifically as deployment/CI rather than general automation

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**.
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams.
- If accurate, replace 1–2 generic tools with stronger implementation language: **Airtable workflow design**, **Power Automate process automation**, **Zapier integrations**.
- Keep only the most relevant/current platforms; consider dropping older/general collaboration tools if space is tight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless central to the role; they may dilute stronger automation tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Because the CV already shows strong email leadership in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and avoid repeating generic channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email marketing, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of generic tool listing: **enterprise newsletter operations**, **member communications**, or **CRM-connected campaign workflows**.
- Keep the newest/most relevant platform first; if Dynamics 365 is current, leave as-is, otherwise reorder by actual recent use.
- Consider renaming the heading to **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms** for clearer positioning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat audience scale here unless tied to a platform-specific capability.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “firsts” from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and recurring video content, and helped establish repeatable digital production workflows.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If available, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement lift, or website traffic during the refresh period.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “Associate Communications Director” entry; keep this item focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats language used in newer roles; specify early-stage process building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, cross-functional support, and the podcast as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; helped translate project work into digital and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more active: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, teams/stakeholders served, or audiences reached.
- Keep this entry lighter than later roles; avoid overemphasizing broad digital leadership that is better demonstrated from 2015 onward.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep it brief here.
- Podcast production is distinct—use that as the main impact point.
